title: Raat ko khana kyun nahi? Ahimsa ka sookshm sach
hooks: Raat ka khana... ahimsa tod deta hai?
Suraj doobte hi... anek jeev jaagte hain

hook_why: Direct question with surprise in first 5 words; mirrors viewer's daily curiosity about Chauvihar

mechanism: Invisible beings contaminate food and water
Cooking and eating harms or ingests them
Daylight eating avoids this invisible violence

claims.claim: Acharanga Sutra prohibits eating after sunset to avoid harming microscopic beings
claims.basis: Acharanga Sutra / Agam source cited in prompt; Jainknowledge.com confirms chauvihar rooted in ahimsa for invisible beings

claims.claim: Jain texts state microorganisms become more active after sunset
claims.basis: Jinsetu.in states 'many micro-organisms (Trasa Jiva) emerge and multiply rapidly after the sun goes down'

claims.claim: Chauvihar means no food and no water after sunset for laypeople
claims.basis: Jainknowledge.com: 'Śvetāmbara: Laypeople commonly keep full chauvihār—no food and no water after sunset'

claims.claim: Monks eat only in daylight, often before noon
claims.basis: Jainknowledge.com: 'Sādhus/sādhvīs of both traditions are stricter: food only in daylight (often before noon), never after sunset'

claims.claim: Circadian rhythm science supports early eating for digestion and sleep
claims.basis: Jinsetu.in: 'Modern science now supports the ancient Jain practice through the study of Circadian Rhythms'
